paper.title_en: Resource-aware QAOA for autoclave batch scheduling in composite manufacturing using QUBO decomposition and parameter transfer
paper.abstract_en: Industrial quantum computing requires problem decompositions that respect near-term resource limits while preserving operational value. This study presents a hybrid classical-quantum workflow for autoclave batch scheduling in composite manufacturing, in which release-time and cure-family logic remain in a classical orchestration layer and each batch-selection decision is encoded as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem. Candidate pools of 4-10 jobs produce 8-14 logical-qubit QAOA subproblems after capacity-slack encoding. Depth-1 and depth-2 QAOA were evaluated using noiseless statevector simulation, with depth-2 parameters trained on four instances per problem size and transferred without re-optimization to six held-out instances per size. For transferred depth-2 QAOA, decoded feasible probability mass decreased from 0.956 at 8 qubits to 0.427 at 14 qubits, while optimal-subset probability decreased from 0.05283 to 0.00150. Comparison with an exact uniform-sampling null showed no consistent optimal-subset concentration advantage for transferred $\text{p}=2$ QAOA, despite exact best-of-4096 recovery across the held-out instances. The estimated sampling budget for a 95% probability of observing the optimum increased from approximately 55 to 2000 shots. In 15 end-to-end synthetic production scenarios containing 24-48 jobs, no statistically significant differences were detected between transferred QAOA and exact per-batch selection or simulated annealing for any reported schedule metric. Relative to greedy selection, transferred QAOA increased mean autoclave utilization by 2.70% points, corresponding to a 3.3% relative increase. This was the only nominally significant paired difference against greedy selection (unadjusted Wilcoxon $\:p=0.029$); other schedule metrics improved directionally but were not statistically significant. All results were obtained using noiseless statevector simulation and establish neither quantum advantage nor hardware-level speedup, but rather a testable quantum-classical integration pathway defined by decomposition, parameter reuse, sampling burden, and classical fallback.
